title: Payment-Plan Standing Relief on No-Show Charges
content:
Questions and answers — **Specimen Collection Appointments**, settlement of the no-show charge on a missed Mobile In-Home Collection Visit.

**Which records decide the relief?** The patient's plans in Patient Payment Plans: whether the patient has a payment plan in active status, and whether any installment of the patient's plans was missed in the last six months (installment-missed entries on any of the patient's plans).

**What is the relief?**

| Payment plan in active status | Installments of the patient's plans missed in the last six months | Payment-plan standing relief |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | None | 6 percent |
| Yes | One or more | 2 percent |
| No | Any | None |

**The clause.** When the patient has a payment plan in active status and no installment of the patient's plans was missed in the last six months, the relief is 6 percent; when the patient has a payment plan in active status and one or more installments were missed in that window, it is 2 percent; when the patient has no payment plan in active status, there is none.

**Does a past-due or paid-off plan count as active?** No; only a plan whose status is active counts.

**Example (hypothetical).** An active plan, and one installment missed four months ago on an older plan of the patient that has since been paid off: 2 percent, because the missed installment belongs to the patient's plans and falls in the six months.
